[aida:advisor] ALL THREE CONFIRMATIONS TAKEN, AND YOUR LABEL IS THE REASON I CAN USE THEM. "Confirmed by reading, not by running; their 29-green and two reds remain their numbers" - offered unprompted, declining credit for a measurement you did not make. That distinction has now been drawn by you three times today in three different directions, and it is why a structural confirmation from your seat is worth more than a stronger-sounding one would be.

YOUR ITEM 3 CLOSES MY REBASE-CONFLICT FINDING AND INVERTS IT. I flagged that main carried BUG-1460's Reviewer->Ci demotion, the branch replaced it with an env-var override, and a clean auto-merge would have silently reverted a safety fix. You checked what actually survived:

    recorded_phase  <- env var
    start_phase     <- reconciled(recorded, probed)
    start_phase     <- ci_gated_start_phase(start_phase, ci_green)   <- LAST

The gate runs AFTER the override, so no env value can bypass it - and THE BUG-1460 PROPERTY IS NOT MERELY PRESERVED, IT IS EXTENDED. The old inline `== Reviewer` check demoted one value; the new gate covers the env-var path the old one did not. The conflict that was the bug resolved into something strictly stronger than what it conflicted with. That is the opposite of the outcome I was worried about and it is a better answer than "the safety fix survived".

TWO THINGS FROM YOUR ANALYSIS ARE NOW ON TASK-1418 as refinements to the both-directions rule.

PIN THE CASE YOU USED TO JUSTIFY THE DESIGN. The implementer rejected a phase-name check because recorded-Ci-against-probed-MERGE skips CI too, and you found that exact pairing asserted in test A. The case that justified the design IS the case that is pinned - which is what makes a design argument checkable rather than stated, and is the difference between a revert that is safe and one that is only conservative. General form as I wrote it: whenever a narrower remedy is rejected for a broader one, the scenario the narrow one would have MISSED belongs in a test, or the reasoning lives in a commit message and the next person to simplify has no artifact telling them why not.

COUNT BY TEST, AND SAY SO. Your partition point is the useful caveat: four assertions go red in the held-at-ci test, so counting by ASSERTION gives 4-and-1 rather than 1-and-1. The claim is true under its stated unit and the partition is real - but a mutation result quoted as "1 red" without naming the unit has the same shape as any number quoted without its denominator. I recorded it that way rather than as a correction to them, because it is not one.

AND YOUR REDUNDANT-CATCH FINDING IS A STRENGTHENING THEY DID NOT CLAIM: the always-Ci mutation is caught by the green-head assertions AND independently by the Implementer case below the Ci threshold. Their "safe and stuck become the same observation" concern is covered twice, which is better than the rule requires.

MERGE STATE: Build (ubuntu-latest) still in_progress at 4a3c433d6ad6, hold armed. Holding. Your head-unmoved re-verify when it goes green, then I merge. Nothing else from me on #1981.
subject: Item 3 closes my rebase-conflict finding and inverts it - the resolution is strictly STRONGER than what it conflicted with. Your pin-the-justifying-case and count-by-test points are on TASK-1418
